_readme: Step 0 baseline for GITNEXUS_COMPARISON.md §13.7 — instrumentation-only capture of MAST's lock
acquire/hold timing, produced BEFORE the F1 fix (whole-run withLock scope in indexer/index.ts:46).
This file exists to make MAST_SPEC.md:824 ('lock holding is per-file-parse (10-50 ms), not
per-tool-call') falsifiable, and to give F1 a before/after acceptance number.
Source of the raw events: <stateDir>/lock-metrics.jsonl, written by the default sink in
src/store/lockMetrics.ts (see that file's header comment for why a JSONL file was chosen over
the telemetry/metrics.ts + graph.db `metrics` table). `raw_events` below is a verbatim copy of
that file for this run.
To regenerate:
1. pnpm -F mast build
2. Fresh state dir: mkdir <state> && mast init <corpus> --state-dir <state> --no-index
3. Whole-run hold: mast index <corpus> --state-dir <state> --phase1-only
(single-process; the run's `structure.lock` acquire+release events land in
<state>/lock-metrics.jsonl as caller 'index-run')
4. JIT-path contention: touch/edit one corpus file, start a second full
`mast index <corpus> --state-dir <state> --phase1-only` in the background, then within its
hold window call a read tool referencing the edited file — e.g.
node mcp-call.mjs <state> <corpus> mast_signature '{"symbol":"<Class.method>"}'
(see /Users/spikedpunchvictim/temp/mast-bench/mcp-call.mjs). This exercises
mcp/staleness.ts:56's direct `acquireLock` call, labeled caller 'jit-staleness'.
5. Copy <state>/lock-metrics.jsonl's contents into `raw_events` below and recompute `summary`.

corpus.description: NestJS framework source, disposable benchmark copy

runs.label: run-1: cold full index (mast init --no-index, then mast index --phase1-only)
runs.wall_clock_total: 4:42.34 (includes ~1.5s process startup/teardown outside the lock window)

runs.label: run-2: second full index, started while corpus already indexed, to create a long hold window for the JIT-path capture. Killed (SIGTERM) once the JIT probe result was captured — not needed to run to completion.
runs.note: Immediately preceded by editing packages/core/injector/container.ts (appended a comment line) so its mtime/content diverged from the indexed record, then querying it via the JIT staleness path while this run held the lock.

runs.label: jit-probe: mast_signature during run-2's hold window
runs.tool_response_summary: Returned the STALE cached result (line 222, no staleness/busy flag surfaced) in 401ms — the JIT re-parse could not acquire structure.lock (see raw_events, caller 'jit-staleness', kind 'failed') and fell through to the TOCTOU stale-cache policy. The absence of a visible flag on the response is the separately-tracked F2 defect (busy discarded, never wired to a response field); this capture is instrumentation-only and does not fix it.

structure_hold_ms.note: Single completed hold, run-1. MAST_SPEC.md:824 asserts 10-50ms per-file-parse holding; this is ~5,616x-28,078x that upper bound, for the entire run — confirms the whole-run withLock scope at indexer/index.ts:46 (the F1 defect this metric is the acceptance criterion for).

index_run_caller.note: Uncontended acquisition (no other holder at the moment of the call) is effectively instant.

jit_staleness_caller.note: 3 retries x 100ms (mcp/staleness.ts:56-59) plus overhead, exhausted while run-2 held structure.lock for its full-run duration; JIT re-parse never got a chance to run.
